Computer Systems

Unit 9 • SL

3 Weeks (9 Lessons) • A1.1.1, A1.1.1, A1.1.2, A1.1.4, A1.1.5, A1.1.7, A1

Unit Overview

of Computer Science Unit Foundation Concepts The core concept is the Architecture of Execution. This unit focuses on the physical reality of the "Stored Program" concept (Von Neumann architecture). Key themes include the Hierarchy of Memory (balancing speed, cost, and capacity), the Orchestration of Instructions (the FDE Cycle), and the Abstraction of Infrastructure via Cloud services.

What You'll Learn

  • A1.1.1 — CPU components: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU). Registers: Program Counter (PC), Memory Address Register (MAR), Memory Data Register (MDR), Accumulator (AC), and Instruction Register (
  • A1.1.1 — System Buses: Data, Address, and Control (Bidirectional vs Unidirectional).
  • A1.1.2 — Role of the GPU: Parallel processing for graphics and non-graphics tasks (AI/simulations).
  • A1.1.4 — Primary Memory: RAM (Volatility), ROM (Non-volatile, BIOS), and Cache hierarchy (L1, L2, L3).
  • A1.1.5 — The Fetch-Decode-Execute (FDE) Cycle mechanics.
  • A1.1.7 — Secondary Storage: HDD (Magnetic), SSD (NAND Flash), eMMC, and Network Attached Storage (NAS/RAID).
  • A1.1.8 — Compression: Lossless (RLE/Statistical redundancy) vs Lossy (Transform coding/Psychovisual redundancy).
  • A1.1.9 — Cloud Computing: SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS models.

Key Terminology

Master these terms to succeed in this unit:

CPU ALU CU PC MAR MDR AC IR Bus Cache Hit/Miss Volatile Non-volatile BIOS NAND Flash RAID RLE Transform Coding SaaS PaaS IaaS

Common Misconceptions

  • Memory vs Storage: Using the terms interchangeably (e.g., "I need more memory on my hard drive").
  • The "Cloud": Thinking the cloud is an abstract "space" rather than a physical server farm managed via virtualisation.
  • Multi-core performance: Assuming a 4-core processor is simply 4x faster than a single core, ignoring software-level threading limitations.
  • Register updates: Believing the PC updates at the end of the cycle rather than immediately after the fetch.

Big Ideas to Consider

  • Abstraction and Knowledge: We interact with computers through high-level GUIs. Does the "hidden" nature of machine code and hardware registers distance us from the "truth" of ho
  • Binary as a Foundation: If all human knowledge can be reduced to 1s and 0s in an Accumulator, is it still "knowledge" or just "data"?
